_source: G1's table (docs/research/G1-artifacts/delta_table.json, BallaSim research, MIT): per-(camera, sequence) residual event offset delta of the released EVIMO2 v2 NPZ, defined by t_vicon = t_event_npz + delta (G1 section 2.4), with its jackknife SE; ms. Rows with a 'remeasured' field were re-measured on 2026-10-10 (tools/evimo2_bench, `evb.py g1fix --write`): their sequences start at GT frame id 1 or 2, and G1 keyed the mask/depth archives by the raw frame id instead of id - first id (R6, G3 t13), so its GT was one frame (16.7 ms) late per unit of first id and its delta about -16.7 ms x first id. They were re-measured over the whole sequence on G1's frame budget (100 or 160 GT frames) with the corrected keys: G1's rule (edges.analyze), then the converged fixed point of its +-2 ms collect window, whose SE is the jackknife SE / (1 - window leverage); where that estimator does not identify delta (not converged, or leverage >= 0.9: two sfm_ll rows), the row holds G1's rule with corrected keys and se_ms null. The other rows keep G1's three-round values and window SEs. The left imo_ll/scene16_d_dyn_test_04 row ('unreliable') keeps G1's value with se_ms null: no estimator identifies it (2026-10-11).

left_camera/imo_ll/scene16_d_dyn_test_04.unreliable: 2026-10-11: G1's value (re-measured exactly by G1's rule, 160 GT frames, first frame id 0) has no converged fixed point: the bench's converged estimator walks to -112.8 ms in 52 rounds. Right (-4.54; converged -3.28 +- 2.27), Samsung (-4.04) and the event scan (+3.5 ms) disagree with it; the mocap is clean (evimo2_gt_quality). se_ms null marks it unusable for timing; the bench treats the span as untimed and clocks.py warns.
